sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: Receivables vs. Revenue Growth: Days sales outstanding moved +214 days over 5 years while revenue compounded -38.8%. Receivables are growing faster than sales, which can flatter revenue recognition and must be watched.
FCF Generation Consistency: Free cash flow was positive in 1 of the last 5 reported years. Repeated FCF deficits mean growth is being funded by the balance sheet rather than by the business.
Current Ratio Liquidity: Current assets cover current liabilities 0.00 times. Liquidity is tight relative to short-term obligations.
Gross Margin Stability: Gross margin varied with a standard deviation of 33.8 percentage points. Margin volatility suggests commodity exposure or weak pricing power.
Operating Margin Stability: Operating margin standard deviation of 56.8 pp indicates cost swings that make forecasting unreliable.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of -8.0% with ROE of -80.0% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
CapEx Intensity Check: Capital expenditure averaged 0.0% of revenue. Capex intensity is unusual for the business model and needs a return check.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 855 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 2 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 5 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded -59.3% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.
